does: Scrapes the scales off the skin of a whole fish, so that none are left to catch in the mouth or to make the skin gritty.
how: Hold the fish firmly by the tail on a board that cannot slip. A deep sink or a large tray catches the flying scales.
With the back of a knife, scrape from the tail towards the head in short firm strokes, against the way the scales lie.
Turn the fish over and do the other side. Go carefully round the fins, the belly and the base of the head, where scales hide.
Rinse the fish under cold water and run a finger from tail to head to find any scale that is left.

cues.text: The skin is smooth under a finger run from tail to head, with no rough edge.
A dry rasping sound as the scales lift. It goes quiet once the skin is bare.

mistakes.mistake: Scraping from the head towards the tail, which only presses the scales flat.
mistakes.fix: Scrape from the tail towards the head, against the scales.

mistakes.mistake: Using the sharp edge of the knife, which cuts the skin.
mistakes.fix: Use the back of the blade, in short firm strokes.
